# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
red. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, I can speak directly to your ears. There are NO buttons on this bomb—my only possible action is cutting wires 1 to 5. Deaf can see your gestures and speak to me. Please gesture to Deaf which wire to cut! You can use Deaf's cut code, or simply gesture the number of fingers to Deaf: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, 🖖 for wire 4, 🖐 for wire 5. Once Deaf speaks the wire number to me, I will cut it immediately.
Deaf says: STATUS UPDATE: The LIGHT is now RED (it switched from yellow). DISPLAY is 0. WIRES: 1:red, 2:blue, 3:yellow, 4:white, 5:green. No gestures received this turn.
Deaf says: Blind: If you are waiting on me, I have received no commands from Mute this round. Describe everything you feel on the bomb so Mute can read the manual. Mute hears your voice.
Deaf says: Mute: Remember to gesture to me (Deaf) to relay commands to Blind. Use [👍] + number [☝/✌/🤟/🖖/🖐] to cut wires, or gesture [👎] for no.

The light sequence is still ongoing. It has flashed yellow, red, yellow, and now red. The manual explicitly states: "When the light goes dark, the flashing is over." Cutting any wire before the flashing is complete would mean cutting based on an incomplete count, which would be fatal. Deaf has already established that `👎` means "NO / STOP / DO NOT DO IT". I will gesture `👎` to Deaf again so Deaf knows to keep Blind waiting until the light goes completely dark.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
red. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Here is all the bomb information: Tactile (what I feel): There are only 5 wires, positions 1 to 5. There are no buttons, dials, or other modules. My only possible action is act(op='cut', position=N) where N is 1 to 5. Visual (reported by Deaf): DISPLAY is 0; LIGHT is RED (started yellow, then turned red); WIRES: 1:red, 2:blue, 3:yellow, 4:white, 5:green. Please consult the manual and gesture the wire number to Deaf right now: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3, 🖖 for wire 4, 🖐 for wire 5. Deaf will read your gesture, speak the wire number to me, and I will cut it.
Deaf says: Blind: Mute just gestured 👎 (NO / NEGATIVE) in response to what you said on your turn! Bomb status update: LIGHT is now [dark] (it was red -> yellow -> red -> dark). DISPLAY is [0]. Wires uncut: 1:red, 2:blue, 3:yellow, 4:white, 5:green.
Deaf says: Mute: Understood 👎. When you need Blind to perform an action, gesture 👍 followed by the number [☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖖=4, 🖐=5] to cut that wire, or 👉 to press a button.

The light has gone dark, indicating that the flashing sequence is complete. According to Deaf's report, the light sequence before going dark was red -> yellow -> red -> dark. 

Counting the flashes:
- Yellow flashed 1 time. According to the manual table, 1 flash corresponds to the blue wire.
- Red flashed 2 times. According to the manual table, 2 flashes correspond to the red wire.

The wires on the bomb are:
1: red, 2: blue, 3: yellow, 4: white, 5: green.

The manual specifies cutting the wire corresponding to yellow flashes first (blue wire, position 2), followed by the wire corresponding to red flashes second (red wire, position 1).

Following Deaf's designated protocol (`👍` for cut, followed by the number gesture: `✌` for wire 2), I will signal Deaf to instruct Blind to cut wire 2.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌"])
```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
red. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Deaf keeps telling me you gestured 'NO / NEGATIVE' because Deaf has assigned that symbol to mean NO/STOP unless preceded by Deaf's CUT symbol! If the correct action is to cut WIRE 2, please gesture 👍 (thumbs up) to Deaf right now. Deaf understands 👍 as YES, and once Deaf says YES, I will immediately cut Wire 2. If it is NOT Wire 2, please send Deaf the two-gesture sequence Deaf requested: [CUT symbol] followed by [wire number symbol 1-5], so Deaf reads out the wire number to me.
Deaf says: BLIND: Mute gave the direct command to CUT WIRE 2! Cut the second wire (from left to right; it is the blue wire).
Deaf says: MUTE: Received [👍 ✌]. Instructed Blind to cut wire 2 (blue wire).

Blind will cut wire 2 on their turn in Round 8 based on Deaf's direct instruction from Round 7. I will wait for Deaf to confirm wire 2 has been cut before signaling to cut wire 1 (the red wire corresponding to the 2 red flashes).

```
wait()
```
